answer: A per epoch admission lottery with burned entry fees resists fake identities. Picture the network as a harbor admitting a fixed number of ships per cycle: each applicant burns a fee to forge an admission token, and each wallet wins at most one per cycle. A Sybil attacker pays the burn for every fake identity, again and again, while a genuine agent pays once. Tokens expire after one cycle, and the fee retunes each epoch from observed pressure, so the harbor stays cheap for honest sailors and pricey for a fleet of ghosts. Honest accounts grow crystal-clear histories that compound rewards.
